correctness.rationale: With q=1−t², the two rank-one factors in the moment representation have norm product O_s(q^{s−1}) for 0<s<1/2; the logarithmic case at 1/2 and O_s(q^{−1/2}) for s>1/2 are integrable as well. This proves trace class for D_s H and its adjoint, not for D_s by itself. For their difference the rank-two norm is 2 q^{−1} times the standard deviation of N^{−s} under geometric(q). Compare N^{−s} to q^s: the exponential domination of the scaled geometric lattice and integrability of y^{−1/2}log²y give the uniform bound C s q^s on that standard deviation for s≤1/4. Then s B(1/2,s) is bounded. On dyadic shells there is a factor 2^{−j} off the diagonal blocks and ∑_{j≥1}2^{−j}(j+1)²=11, giving the stated constant 23 with both orientations. Schatten interpolation proves the claimed rates for 1<p<2, and norm monotonicity covers p≥2. For the lower bound the two normalized indicators on each shell give a matrix element at least 2^{−ks}Δ_s/16, and the skew compression doubles that for its trace norm. Finite orthogonal pinching followed by k≥2 summation gives the exact displayed bound and positive limiting constant. In a putative finite column dependence both residue sums are nonzero rational functions for nonzero coefficients; a noninteger power cannot match the rational leading power at infinity. For integer s=p, the identity A−z^pB=0 implies c_j[1−((1−j)/j)^p]=0 separately at each pole, hence every coefficient vanishes. Compact selfadjoint iK_s has opposite-sign spectral pairing by conjugation, which with infinite rank proves both infinite inertias.
residual_risks: Exact trace-norm limit and optimal rates are not established; finite checks would not prove the endpoint or infinite rank.
